text: A girl named June found a blue feather and put it in a book so she would not lose it.
The horse drank from the stream and then walked back to the barn with the farmer.
He tried to stack the cups, but they fell. He tried again, slower, and they stayed up.
The baby laughed when the dog licked her hand. Mom said the dog was being gentle.
Clouds hid the sun and the path got dark. They turned on a lamp and kept walking.
Pia drew a house with a red roof. Her brother added a tree and a yellow bird.
The ice melted in the glass. Water ran down the side and made a ring on the table.
A squirrel hid a nut under a leaf. In winter it came back and dug until it found it.
They waited for the bus in the rain. When it came, they shook their coats and sat down.
The old clock ticked in the hall. Nobody was awake except the cat on the stairs.
Leo learned to tie his shoes. He was proud, and he tied them again to show his dad.
The soup was too hot, so they blew on it. After a minute they could eat it.
A whale rose from the water and then slipped under again. The boat rocked a little.
She lost a tooth and put it under her pillow. In the morning a coin was there.
The kids built a fort from chairs and a blanket. They whispered so the walls would not fall.
Wind blew the leaves into a pile. Then it blew them apart, and they had to rake again.
The teacher read a story. When it ended, the class asked her to read one more page.
A candle burned on the table until the wax made a small white lake around it.
They planted a tree by the fence. Years later it made shade for the whole yard.
The fox stopped at the edge of the field. It listened, then ran into the dark trees.
Nora found a smooth stone in the creek and kept it in her pocket all day.
The kite string slipped. Dad caught it, and they sent the kite up again.
A robin built a nest on the porch light. The family left the light off.
He poured milk too fast and it splashed. He wiped the table with a cloth.
The library was quiet. She opened a book about ships and forgot the time.
They raced to the corner. The one in red shoes won and waited for the rest.
Grandma's cookies cooled on a rack. The dog sat under the table and hoped.
A storm knocked a branch onto the path. They stepped over it on the way home.
The baby pointed at the moon. Her sister said it was far, far away.
He practiced the song until he could play it without looking at his hands.
The ferry blew its horn. People held the rail as the dock slid away.
She tied a ribbon on the gift and wrote her friend's name in big letters.
The pond froze at the edges. Ducks stayed in the open water in the middle.
They counted the stairs. There were twelve, and the last one creaked.
A balloon got loose at the fair. It rose until it was a red dot.
The mailman waved. The dog barked once, then sat and wagged.
He mixed red and yellow paint. The paper turned orange, and he smiled.
The tent flap stuck. Mom unzipped it, and the morning air came in.
A turtle crossed the road. Cars waited until it reached the grass.
She saved a seat on the bench. When her friend arrived they shared the snack.
The clock in the kitchen was five minutes fast. They still caught the bus.
He dropped a penny in the fountain and watched it sink.
The cat knocked a spool of thread off the table. It rolled under the chair.
They picked blueberries until the pail was heavy. Their fingers were purple.
A lighthouse blinked over the water. The boat steered toward the light.
The snow stuck to his mittens. He clapped them and the snow fell off.
She read the sign twice, then pushed the door and heard a small bell.
The horse lowered its head so the girl could touch its nose.
They built a bridge of blocks across the rug. The toy car drove over it.
Dad lit the stove. The pan hissed when the butter hit it.
A moth landed on the screen. The boy watched its wings and did not touch it.
The class planted beans in cups. Two days later a green hook appeared.
She lost her glove and found it on the fence where she had climbed.
The river was loud after the rain. They stayed on the high path.
He folded the map wrong, then folded it again until it fit in his pocket.
The puppy learned to sit. It got a small piece of cheese and sat again.
They hung the wet coats by the door. Water dripped onto an old towel.
A star showed before the sky was dark. She pointed and her brother looked.
The baker gave them the end of the loaf. It was still warm.
He zippered his jacket to his chin. The wind pushed, and he leaned into it.
The goldfish swam in a circle. She sprinkled food and the fish rose.
They wrote their names in the sand. A wave took the letters away.
Mom hummed while she swept. The broom found a button under the rug.
The train whistle was long. They counted the cars until the last one passed.
A spider sat in the corner of the window. They left the web alone.
He carried the eggs one at a time. None of them cracked.
The swing went high. She dragged her feet and the swing slowed down.
They shared one umbrella. Their shoulders got wet, and they laughed.
The owl called from the pine. The yard went still for a moment.
She buttoned the doll's coat. The doll sat on the shelf and faced the room.
The ice cream melted down the cone. He turned it and licked the drip.
A key was under the mat. It opened the shed, and the bikes were inside.
They lined up for the slide. The smallest went first and came down grinning.
The radio played a slow song. Grandpa tapped the table with two fingers.
She watered the plant until water came out the bottom of the pot.
The hill was steep. They walked sideways and held hands.
A paper boat lasted until the middle of the puddle, then tipped.
He set the alarm and put the clock across the room so he had to stand up.
The chickens rushed the fence when she brought the grain.
They found a four-leaf clover and pressed it in a heavy book.
The flashlight made a circle on the tent wall. They made shadow rabbits.
A truck backed up with a beep. The kids moved their bikes off the driveway.
She tied the apron strings in a bow. Flour was already on her cheek.
The creek was cold. He stepped in, yelped, and stepped right back out.
They saved the last piece of cake. In the morning it was still there.
The door stuck in the heat. Dad lifted it a little and it swung free.
A jay stole a peanut from the feeder and flew to the oak.
He counted his coins. He had enough for one postcard and one stamp.
The curtains moved although the window was shut. The vent under them was on.
They walked the long way home so they could pass the house with the big dog.
The chalk broke in her hand. She used the short piece and kept drawing.
A bell rang at noon. Workers sat on the curb and opened their lunches.
The puppy slept with its nose on his shoe. He did not move his foot.
She closed the book on her finger so she would not lose the page.
The fog hid the far trees. By lunch the sun had burned it off.
They stacked firewood under the eaves. The top pieces were dry to the touch.
He waved at the plane. It was too high to wave back, and he knew that.
The soup needed salt. She added a pinch, tasted it, and nodded.
A marble rolled down the hall and stopped against the closet door.
The moon was thin. She said it looked like a bite taken out of a cookie.
